title: Finite-presentation algebraic-space descent over qcqs scheme limits
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact; a morphism is quasi-compact when its pullback by any affine scheme has quasi-compact source. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A closed immersion is representable and is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]. An affine morphism is representable and has affine source after every affine scheme test. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $J$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(T_j)_{j\in J}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, and $T=\varprojlim_j T_j$. Every finitely presented algebraic space $Y\to T$ is isomorphic over $T$ to $Y_j\times_{T_j}T$ for a finitely presented algebraic space $Y_j\to T_j$ at some $j$. For finitely presented $Y_j,Z_j$ over $T_j$, every $T$-morphism between their pullbacks descends to a $T_l$-morphism between their pullbacks to some $l\ge j$. Two such stage morphisms whose pullbacks to $T$ agree become equal after pullback to some later common stage. These assertions hold without an affineness assumption on the schemes $T_j$.

source.place: Tag 07SK (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), restricted to qcqs scheme bases, including descent of objects, morphisms and equality

proof.text: Fix an index $0$ and restrict to the cofinal directed tail $J_{\ge0}$. A cone on this tail extends uniquely to the original diagram: for $a\in J$ choose $b\ge a,0$ and compose its $b$-component with $T_b\to T_a$; a common upper bound shows independence. Thus its limit is still $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $T\to T_0$ is affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2) shows that $T$ is qcqs. Base change preserves finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], so all finite-stage pullbacks below remain finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 07SK (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), preliminary tail and finiteness checks; scheme limit Tag 01YX

proof.text: Let $Y\to T$ be finitely presented. By [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source], $Y$ is qcqs. Choose an affine scheme atlas $q:W\to Y$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. The chart criterion [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test], with identity target chart $T\to T$, makes $W\to T$ locally finitely presented. The affine scheme $W$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; scheme permanence [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $W\to T$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence finitely presented. By [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation], $R=W\times_YW$ is a scheme, its projections $s,t$ are etale, $(s,t)$ is a monomorphism and an equivalence relation, and $Y$ is its sheaf quotient.

source.place: Tag 07SK, first paragraph, presentation Y=W/R; Tag 03H6 and Tag 0262

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-fibre-product], $R=W\times_YW$ is qcqs. Since $s:R\to W$ is etale, it is locally finitely presented by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Composition [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition] with $W\to T$ makes $R\to T$ locally finitely presented. Its source is qcqs and $T$ is quasi-separated, so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) gives the two other finiteness conditions. Thus both schemes $W,R$ are finitely presented over the possibly nonaffine scheme $T$. This supplies the finiteness check needed before scheme descent; $R$ need not be affine.

source.place: Tag 07SK, first paragraph, the finiteness details before invoking Tag 01ZM; Tag 073B and Tag 01TR

proof.text: Apply clauses (1) and (2) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to the schemes $W,R$ and the maps $s,t$. At a common stage $i$ this gives finitely presented schemes $W_i,R_i$ over $T_i$ and maps $s_i,t_i:R_i\rightrightarrows W_i$ with the given limiting presentation. Directedness supplies common stages, and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3) preserves their finite presentation on enlargement. Its (2) makes every such $W_i,R_i$ qcqs. The hypotheses of the scheme theorem hold because every $T_i$ is qcqs and the transitions are affine. No affineness of $T_i$ is used.

source.place: Tag 07SK, first paragraph: descend presentation schemes and maps using Tag 01ZM

proof.text: We check the local finiteness hypotheses for property descent. A map between schemes finitely presented over $T_i$ is locally finitely presented. Indeed, near any source point choose an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset T_i$, an affine target open over it, and an affine source open mapping into that target. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] their rings have finite presentations $C=A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]/J$ and $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/K$. If the given map sends $y_a$ to $p_a(x)$, then $B=C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(K(x),y_a-p_a(x))$. These are finitely many relations by [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], proving local finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and local finite type by forgetting the relations. Scheme products of finitely presented objects over $T_i$ are finitely presented, using base change [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3) and composition [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](d). Thus this applies to $s_i,t_i$ and $j_i=(s_i,t_i):R_i\to W_i\times_{T_i}W_i$; their sources and targets are qcqs by permanence (2).

source.place: Tag 07SK, property-descent hypotheses; Morphisms Tags 01TQ and 02FV, written finite-algebra calculation

proof.text: The limit maps $s,t$ are etale and $j=(s,t)$ is a monomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale] to $s_i,t_i$ and [lem-weil-pbc-descend-monomorphism] to $j_i$ to make these properties hold at one later stage. All three applications have qcqs base, source and target; the necessary local finite presentation or local finite type was checked in step 5. Etaleness persists on enlargement by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Monomorphisms persist too: two maps into a pullback with equal composites into its target have equal composites into its original source, by monicity, and equal base components, hence are equal by the pullback universal property.

source.place: Tag 07SK, eventual etaleness and monomorphism; scheme Tags 07RP, 07RQ

proof.text: The relation axioms must also descend. At the limit the kernel pair has $e:W\to R$, $v:R\to R$ and $c:R\times_{t,W,s}R\to R$ given by $w\mapsto(w,w)$, $(w_1,w_2)\mapsto(w_2,w_1)$ and $((w_1,w_2),(w_2,w_3))\mapsto(w_1,w_3)$. By step 5, $s_i,t_i$ are locally finitely presented, and by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) they are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Consequently $P_i=R_i\times_{t_i,W_i,s_i}R_i$ is finitely presented over $T_i$, by its (3) and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](d). Clause (2) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] descends $e,v,c$ to a common later stage. Clause (3) makes the finitely many equations $s_ie_i=t_ie_i=\mathrm{id}$, $s_iv_i=t_i$, $t_iv_i=s_i$, $s_ic_i=s_i\operatorname{pr}_1$, $t_ic_i=t_i\operatorname{pr}_2$ hold there. On points of every test scheme these exhibit reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity. Together with monicity of $j_i$, they make $R_i\rightrightarrows W_i$ an etale equivalence relation.

source.place: Tag 07SK, before setting Y_i=W_i/R_i: explicit descent of the equivalence-relation witnesses and equations by Tag 01ZM

proof.text: By [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient], the sheaf quotient $Y_i=W_i/R_i$ is an algebraic space, with a representable surjective etale atlas $W_i\to Y_i$ whose kernel pair is $R_i$. Since $W_i,R_i$ are qcqs, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $R_i\to W_i$ quasi-compact. Hence [lem-sfb-space-qs-atlas-criterion] makes $Y_i$ quasi-separated. It is quasi-compact: its atlas has quasi-compact source, as in the definition in the item; equivalently, continuity and surjectivity of the point map in [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] pull an open cover back to $W_i$, where a finite subcover exists, and surjectivity makes the same finite family cover $Y_i$. The chart criterion [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] applied to $W_i\to Y_i$ and the identity chart on $T_i$ gives local finite presentation of $Y_i\to T_i$. Finally [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of this morphism because $Y_i$ is qcqs and $T_i$ is quasi-separated. Thus $Y_i\to T_i$ is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 07SK, quotient finite presentation over X_i; Tags 07S4, 0410, 073B

proof.text: Base change of this atlas to $T$ is an etale surjective atlas with kernel pair $R$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation], both $Y$ and $Y_i\times_{T_i}T$ are the sheaf quotient of the same relation $R\rightrightarrows W$. The universal property of [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] gives maps in both directions induced by the identity on $W$. Each composite restricts to the identity on $W$, so quotient uniqueness makes it the identity. The maps respect $T$, since their composites to $T$ agree on $W$, again by quotient uniqueness. This proves the required isomorphism over $T$ and object descent.

Fix finitely presented $Y_i,Z_i$ over $T_i$ and a $T$-map $\alpha:Y\to Z$ of their pullbacks. By [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source], $Y_i$ is qcqs. Choose an affine surjective etale atlas $W_i\to Y_i$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. By [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation] its kernel pair $R_i$ is a scheme and $Y_i=W_i/R_i$. The scheme $W_i$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; then [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-fibre-product] makes $R_i$ qcqs. Put $W_k=W_i\times_{T_i}T_k$ and $R_k=R_i\times_{T_i}T_k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit] these systems have affine transitions and limits $W,R$. Their maps to $W_i,R_i$ are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1), so its (3) and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2) make every stage qcqs. Apply [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test] over the fixed scheme $T_i$ with target $Z_i$ to $W\to Y\xrightarrow{\alpha}Z\to Z_i$. Since $Z_i\to T_i$ is locally finitely presented, this descends to $b_k:W_k\to Z_i$ at some $k\ge i$.

source.place: Tag 07SK, full faithfulness paragraph: descend the atlas map using Tag 04AK

proof.text: The maps $b_ks_k,b_kt_k:R_k\to Z_i$ agree after pullback to $R$. Apply the injectivity clause of [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test] to the qcqs scheme system $(R_l)_{l\ge k}$ to make them equal at a later stage $l$. Pair $b_l$ with the structure map into $T_l$ to obtain a $T_l$-map $W_l\to Z_l$, equalizing $R_l\rightrightarrows W_l$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], this is the kernel pair of the pullback atlas $W_l\to Y_l$. By [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation] and [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient], the equalizing map factors uniquely through $\alpha_l:Y_l\to Z_l$. It respects $T_l$ because its composite to $T_l$ and the structure map of $Y_l$ agree after $W_l\to Y_l$, so quotient uniqueness makes them equal. Its base change is $\alpha$, since both maps agree on $W$. Thus every morphism descends; the scheme $R_l$ need not be affine.

source.place: Tag 07SK, full faithfulness paragraph: equality on overlaps and quotient factorization

proof.text: For two stage maps $a_i,b_i:Y_i\to Z_i$ whose pullbacks agree, restrict them to the affine atlas $W_i\to Y_i$ from step 10. Injectivity in [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test] makes these two maps $W_i\to Z_i$ equal after some base change $T_l\to T_i$. The pulled-back atlas presents $Y_l$ as $W_l/R_l$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation]. Quotient uniqueness [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] therefore makes $a_l=b_l$. If the maps start at different stages, first move them to a common stage by directedness. This is precisely the eventual-equality assertion. All three conclusions were obtained for qcqs, possibly nonaffine stage bases.

Mathematics: the item is 07SK restricted to qcqs scheme bases, and its three clauses are not weakened. Steps 1-3 put W and R in fp over a possibly nonaffine T: 06G5, 03H6, the chart test with V=T, scheme qcqs permanence, 073B(3). Steps 4-6 use 01ZM(1),(2), and 07RP and 07RQ, whose qcqs and lfp/lft hypotheses come from step 5. I checked step 5's algebra: A[y,x]/(J,K,y-p) is A[x]/K because J(p) lies in K. Step 7 descends e, v, c; I checked its six equations against t(r1)=s(r2); this gives the 02WW equivalence-relation hypothesis, which the source leaves implicit. Step 8: 02WW, plus 07S4 via s_i qc; qc through the continuous surjection of points; lfp by the chart test; qcqs by 073B. Step 9: both Y and Y_i x T are W/R; the isomorphism is over T. Steps 10-12 use 04AK/0CP4 over S=T_i, which does not require fp stages; the factored map is over T_l and its base change is alpha, checked componentwise in Z_i x T; equality via quotient uniqueness. Edge cases: singleton J, empty Y, nonseparated T_i with no affine intersections assumed. Duplicates: lem-sfb-fp-space-limit-category is the affine-base special case, not a duplicate; I found no other qcqs version.
